data.content_ref: inline:The claim asserts the large service is 'strictly more resilient' because internal redundancy 'eliminates single points of failure,' but its own countercondition admits the monolith's unified control plane can be a single point of failure. A system that can exhibit a single point of failure cannot have 'eliminated' single points of failure. The unconditional 'strictly more resilient' claim is thus directly contradicted by a conceded failure mode, and no condition is placed on the claim to restrict it to architectures lacking a unified control plane.
